chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Recent work with veterans like Little Brother Montgomery and Art Hodes
summary: Saunders explains he can choose jobs for artistic reasons and finds honor in playing with older musicians.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: What kind of work have you been getting the last few years? I heard you with Little Brother Montgomery and (unintelligible) Art Hodes.
Right, right, well, it's been a

combination, and this is what I say about the freedom, being able to accept or reject whatever you want. And you get into the position that you can do that, which -- you're not just -- it's not just totally a bread and butter issue. It's an artistic issue with you.

And then, it's also -- you're searching. Just like I said before, music is a circle and it goes around and around and it never stops. And then, at this age, you're still searching for different things, and you listen to the different people from different areas -- eras. So it's rewarding, to be able to play with these guys.
I mean, I feel that it's really an honor to play with them, because each one of them has something to say, and they said it well earlier, otherwise they wouldn't be here today.
